integration_sequence.merge_scope: design artifacts and guards only; no source-code merge

pre_cutover_binding_model.PRE_CUTOVER_BINDING_AUTHORITY_SOURCE: the existing legacy runtime lifecycle authority after deterministic legacy validation; the shadow graph supplies diagnostic evidence only
pre_cutover_binding_model.candidate_count_rule: candidate_count is computed after deterministic validity filtering, but candidate_count=1 never transfers binding authority from the legacy runtime to the shadow graph
pre_cutover_binding_model.shadow_graph_role: non-authoritative read model until successful explicit cutover
pre_cutover_binding_model.pre_cutover_binding_rule: runtime binding remains on the legacy authority; a valid shadow candidate may be reported, never selected as the authoritative target

post_cutover_binding_model.BINDING_AUTHORITY_SOURCE: the canonical durable Subject Graph after the successful authority flip
post_cutover_binding_model.legacy_pointer_role: compatibility and projection lookup only; pointers cannot override, select, or replace a canonical graph Subject
post_cutover_binding_model.unique_candidate_rule: one valid graph candidate still requires materialized Decision, authority, revision, and predecessor validity
post_cutover_binding_model.post_cutover_binding_rule: binding enumerates and validates canonical durable graph records; stale pointers are repairable projections, not authority

candidate_validity_contract.many_candidate_rule: deterministic validity may expose many candidates for evidence, but neither pre-cutover binding nor post-cutover binding may reduce many to one heuristically

ambiguity_reconciliation.migration_context: legacy identity evidence is non-unique or unmigratable and cannot mint a canonical Subject without an explicit semantic choice
ambiguity_reconciliation.runtime_context: more than one valid canonical binding candidate remains after deterministic validity filtering
ambiguity_reconciliation.followup_rule: later runtime mechanics cannot silently repair or reinterpret an unresolved migration semantic ambiguity

bounded_result_taxonomy.WHEN: no canonical durable Subject exists for the requested identity or lineage
bounded_result_taxonomy.RECOVERY: do not fabricate a Subject; safe diagnosis remains available

bounded_result_taxonomy.WHEN: migration evidence exists but identity candidates are non-unique or unmigratable
bounded_result_taxonomy.RECOVERY: do not mint a Subject or infer a winner; preserve evidence and await explicit semantic choice

bounded_result_taxonomy.WHEN: a canonical durable Subject exists but its current pointer or projection is missing or stale
bounded_result_taxonomy.RECOVERY: rebuild the projection deterministically from the canonical graph without graph mutation

bounded_result_taxonomy.WHEN: a candidate exists but the semantic Decision prerequisite for the requested followup is not materialized
bounded_result_taxonomy.RECOVERY: do not infer intent or create a semantic followup; report the missing prerequisite

bounded_result_taxonomy.WHEN: multiple valid runtime candidates remain after deterministic validity filtering
bounded_result_taxonomy.RECOVERY: do not select between candidates; require an explicit semantic choice

projection_recovery_contract.PROJECTION_REBUILD_REQUIRES_SEMANTIC_CHO: no when the canonical source is uniquely deterministic; an ambiguous or invalid graph is not repairable by guessing
projection_recovery_contract.rebuild_scope: deterministically derive current_* projections from one already-valid canonical Subject
projection_recovery_contract.rebuild_effect: mechanical projection repair only; no new Subject, edge, Decision, authority, or lifecycle transition
projection_recovery_contract.ambiguous_graph_behavior: an ambiguous or invalid canonical graph is not repairable by guessing; leave the projection unrepaired and return NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE or a bounded invalid-state result, and never guess
projection_recovery_contract.replay_rule: replaying the same rebuild converges to the same projection and duplicates no semantic effect

cutover_recovery_boundary.cutover_boundary: only an explicit authorized transition may atomically make the validated Durable Subject Graph authoritative

failed_pre_flip_cutover.legacy_authority: remains sole lifecycle and binding authority
failed_pre_flip_cutover.binding_behavior: must not switch to graph candidates

post_flip_projection_failure.graph_authority: remains sole lifecycle and binding authority
post_flip_projection_failure.projection_behavior: pointer publication may be retried or rebuilt mechanically from graph authority

cutover_recovery_boundary.cutover_replay: a successful replay returns already_cut_over or an equivalent bounded result and performs no second authority transition

pointer_phase_model.POINTER_READ_ROLE: legacy operational lookup authority for the existing runtime only; not canonical Subject identity authority
pointer_phase_model.POINTER_WRITE_ROLE: existing legacy runtime authoritative write path; no authoritative shadow graph write
pointer_phase_model.GRAPH_AUTHORITY: shadow graph is non-authoritative diagnostic evidence
pointer_phase_model.BINDING_AUTHORITY: legacy runtime lifecycle authority; shadow candidates cannot authoritatively bind

pointer_phase_model.POINTER_READ_ROLE: legacy reads support comparison while the explicit transition is serialized
pointer_phase_model.POINTER_WRITE_ROLE: no dual-authoritative write; publication is held at the explicit transition boundary
pointer_phase_model.GRAPH_AUTHORITY: not authoritative until the successful explicit authority flip
pointer_phase_model.BINDING_AUTHORITY: legacy until the flip, then canonical graph after the flip

pointer_phase_model.POINTER_WRITE_ROLE: projection publisher or bounded mechanical rebuild only; never lifecycle authority
pointer_phase_model.GRAPH_AUTHORITY: canonical durable Subject Graph is sole lifecycle authority
pointer_phase_model.BINDING_AUTHORITY: canonical durable Subject Graph; legacy pointers cannot override it

pointer_global_invariants.pre_cutover_qualification: a legacy pointer may be operationally authoritative inside the legacy runtime before cutover, without becoming canonical Subject authority

readonly_boundary.diagnostic_rule: read-only Host diagnosis may report evidence, authority phase, ambiguity, and projection drift without lifecycle mutation or forced Subject binding
readonly_boundary.mutation_boundary: diagnosis cannot mint a Subject, select semantics, flip authority, or repair a projection unless a separate bounded recovery operation is authorized

idempotency_cross_contract.replay_rule: replay may re-read or converge mechanical state, but never creates a second authority, Subject, edge, Decision, or semantic followup effect
idempotency_cross_contract.cutover_once_rule: authority flips at most once and a successful replay cannot create a second transition
idempotency_cross_contract.projection_once_rule: projection rebuild is deterministic and replay-safe
idempotency_cross_contract.binding_once_rule: binding recovery reuses an existing semantic effect and never duplicates it

cross_scenarios.NAME: pre-cutover shadow graph has one candidate
cross_scenarios.given: before cutover, the shadow graph contains one structurally valid candidate and candidate_count=1 after deterministic validity filtering
cross_scenarios.expected: candidate is available for comparison and diagnostics only; it cannot authoritatively bind because PRE_CUTOVER_SHADOW_GRAPH_CAN_AUTHORITATIVELY_BIND=no, so binding authority remains legacy

cross_scenarios.NAME: pre-cutover migration has two valid identity candidates
cross_scenarios.given: migration evidence yields two valid identity candidates and no deterministic semantic winner
cross_scenarios.when: migration and runtime binding are evaluated
cross_scenarios.expected: MIGRATION_REQUIRES_SEMANTIC_CHOICE with semantic class NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE; runtime binding cannot collapse the candidates
cross_scenarios.authority: legacy runtime remains authority; shadow is diagnostic

cross_scenarios.NAME: post-cutover graph Subject with stale pointer
cross_scenarios.given: after cutover, the canonical graph has one valid Subject and the current_* pointer is missing or stale
cross_scenarios.when: binding performs canonical discovery and bounded recovery
cross_scenarios.expected: graph Subject remains discoverable, result is PROJECTION_STALE_RECONCILABLE, and projection is rebuilt deterministically without semantic escalation

cross_scenarios.NAME: post-cutover graph has two valid semantic candidates
cross_scenarios.given: after cutover, deterministic validity filtering leaves two valid canonical Subject candidates
cross_scenarios.when: binding or projection recovery evaluates the candidates
cross_scenarios.expected: NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE; projection rebuild cannot select between multiple semantic Subjects and the graph is not changed

cross_scenarios.NAME: cutover fails before authority flip
cross_scenarios.given: cutover validation or publication fails before the authority flip
cross_scenarios.expected: legacy remains sole binding authority, shadow graph remains non-authoritative diagnostic evidence, and binding does not switch to graph

cross_scenarios.NAME: cutover succeeds but pointer publication fails
cross_scenarios.given: the explicit authority flip succeeds and graph authority is durable, but pointer projection publication fails
cross_scenarios.expected: graph remains binding authority, valid graph Subjects remain discoverable, and mechanical projection recovery is allowed without changing authority
cross_scenarios.semantic_effect: authority transition already completed; projection repair only

cross_scenarios.NAME: unmigratable legacy evidence exists
cross_scenarios.given: legacy evidence is incomplete, conflicting, or non-unique and cannot establish a canonical identity
cross_scenarios.expected: recovery may preserve evidence and diagnose, but may not invent a Subject or resolve UNMIGRATABLE or NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE by heuristic inference
cross_scenarios.authority: legacy until explicit cutover; no invented graph authority

cross_scenarios.NAME: safe Host diagnostic during migration ambiguity
cross_scenarios.given: migration identity is ambiguous while a safe read-only Host diagnostic is requested
cross_scenarios.when: the diagnostic plane evaluates the request
cross_scenarios.expected: safe independent diagnosis remains available; MIGRATION_AMBIGUITY_BLOCKS_SAFE_READONLY_DIAGNOSIS=no and no Subject binding is forced

cross_scenarios.NAME: replayed successful cutover
cross_scenarios.given: the explicit cutover has already completed successfully
cross_scenarios.when: the same cutover request is replayed
cross_scenarios.expected: returns_already_cut_over_or_equivalent_bounded_result; CUTOVER_REPLAY_CREATES_SECOND_AUTHORITY_TRANSITION=no and there is no second authority transition

a6_handoff.authorization_scope: integrated design proof only; do not start M3-A6, M3-B, or any runtime implementation
